name: Gluten-Free
meta_description: Tested gluten-free recipes for every meal, labelled honestly: every ingredient qualifies, and oats are always certified gluten-free.
intro: Every recipe here is gluten-free as written — no hidden flour, and oats only when they're certified gluten-free. Recipes that need one swap are marked “GF option”, so you always know where you stand.
guide_title: Tips for cooking gluten-free at home

guide.title: Read every label
guide.text: Stock cubes, spice blends, soy sauce and baking powder can all contain wheat. Look for a gluten-free label rather than guessing.

guide.title: Use certified oats
guide.text: Oats are often processed alongside wheat. Only oats labelled certified gluten-free are safe for a gluten-free diet.

guide.title: Bake with naturally gluten-free flours
guide.text: Almond flour, buckwheat and oat flour bring flavour as well as structure — great in brownies, pancakes and muffins.

guide.title: Keep things separate
guide.text: Use a clean board, toaster and colander for gluten-free cooking if someone at your table has coeliac disease.

faq.question: Are oats gluten-free?
faq.answer: Oats don't contain gluten, but most are contaminated with wheat during processing. Only certified gluten-free oats are safe, so our recipes say so explicitly.

faq.question: What does “GF option” mean?
faq.answer: The recipe becomes gluten-free with one swap, such as gluten-free bread or certified oats. The swap is listed next to the ingredient.

faq.question: Is rice gluten-free?
faq.answer: Yes, all plain rice is naturally gluten-free, including brown, basmati and glutinous rice.

name: Vegan
meta_description: Plant-based vegan recipes made from whole, everyday ingredients — tested at home, many of them gluten-free too.
intro: Plant-based recipes made from whole, everyday ingredients — no hard-to-find substitutes. Every recipe here is fully vegan, and many are gluten-free too, so they work for mixed tables and weeknight cooking alike.
guide_title: Tips for cooking vegan at home

guide.title: Build every plate around a protein
guide.text: Chickpeas, lentils, tofu and beans keep meals filling. Start with one and build the vegetables and grains around it.

guide.title: Lean on pantry flavour
guide.text: Toasted spices, tahini, miso, lemon and good olive oil add the depth that butter or cheese might bring elsewhere.

guide.title: Use coconut milk and cashews for creaminess
guide.text: Full-fat coconut milk works in curries and soups; blended soaked cashews make a neutral cream for pasta and sauces.

guide.title: Check labels for hidden animal products
guide.text: Stock cubes, some breads and certain sugars can contain dairy or egg. Our labels only go on recipes where every ingredient qualifies.

faq.question: How do vegans get enough protein?
faq.answer: Legumes, tofu, tempeh, nuts, seeds and whole grains all add up. Our High-Protein label marks recipes with a protein-rich base.

faq.question: Are all vegan recipes gluten-free?
faq.answer: No. Bread, pasta, soy sauce and regular oats contain gluten. Look for the Gluten-Free label, or “GF option” when a swap is needed.

faq.question: What can I use instead of eggs in baking?
faq.answer: A flax egg (1 tbsp ground flaxseed plus 3 tbsp water) works in most muffins and pancakes. Mashed banana adds binding and sweetness.

name: Healthy
meta_description: Healthy recipes built on whole foods: mostly plant-based, minimally processed and easy to cook on a weeknight.
intro: Our healthy collection is built on whole foods: mostly plant-based, minimally processed and full of vegetables, legumes and whole grains. It's an editorial collection, not a diet claim — check each recipe's labels for gluten-free or vegan.

guide.title: Whole foods first
guide.text: Vegetables, legumes, whole grains, nuts and seeds make up most of every plate.

guide.title: Minimal processing
guide.text: We cook from simple ingredients and keep ready-made sauces and refined sugar to a minimum.

guide.title: Satisfying portions
guide.text: Fibre and protein keep you full — no tiny servings or calorie counting.

faq.question: Is “healthy” a diet label?
faq.answer: No. It's an editorial collection. For dietary needs, use the Gluten-Free, Vegan, Vegetarian, Dairy-Free or High-Protein labels.

faq.question: Do you show nutrition information?
faq.answer: Not yet. We'd rather show nothing than numbers we haven't checked carefully.

faq.question: Are healthy recipes always vegan?
faq.answer: Mostly plant-based, but some include eggs or cheese. Each recipe shows its diet labels.

name: Breakfast
meta_description: Easy gluten-free, vegan and healthy breakfast recipes — from make-ahead overnight oats to 20-minute pancakes.
intro: Breakfasts that are quick on weekdays and a little special at weekends. Many can be made the night before, and every one is clearly labelled for gluten-free and vegan diets.

guide.title: Prep the night before
guide.text: Overnight oats and pancake batter can be made ahead, so mornings are just assembly.

guide.title: Add protein
guide.text: Eggs, yogurt, nut butter or seeds help a breakfast last until lunch.

guide.title: Keep ripe fruit on hand
guide.text: Spotty bananas and frozen berries sweeten breakfasts without added sugar.

faq.question: Can I make overnight oats gluten-free?
faq.answer: Yes — use certified gluten-free oats. That's why we mark the recipe “GF option”.

faq.question: How long do overnight oats keep?
faq.answer: Up to 3 days in the fridge. Add fresh fruit on the day.

faq.question: Can pancakes be frozen?
faq.answer: Yes. Layer with baking paper and freeze for up to 2 months; reheat in a toaster.

name: Lunch
meta_description: Gluten-free and vegan lunch recipes that pack well — soups, grain bowls and salads.
intro: Soups, grain bowls and salads that taste good on day two. These lunches pack well for work and most can be made in one batch on Sunday.

guide.title: Dress at the last minute
guide.text: Keep dressings in a separate jar so salads stay crisp.

guide.title: Batch the base
guide.text: Cook a pot of grains or soup at the weekend and vary the toppings each day.

guide.title: Think in layers
guide.text: Wet ingredients at the bottom, greens on top — then shake into a bowl.

faq.question: How long does lentil soup keep?
faq.answer: Up to 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

faq.question: Can I eat quinoa bowls cold?
faq.answer: Yes — they're designed to be eaten cold or at room temperature.

faq.question: Are your lunches gluten-free?
faq.answer: Most are. Check the labels on each recipe card.

name: Dinner
meta_description: Weeknight gluten-free and vegan dinner recipes — curries, roasted vegetable salads and protein bowls.
intro: Weeknight dinners that come together in under an hour, mostly from the pantry. Curries, roasted vegetables and protein-packed bowls — each one clearly labelled.

guide.title: Start the slow bit first
guide.text: Get onions, rice or a roasting tray going before you chop anything else.

guide.title: Stock a flavour shelf
guide.text: Canned chickpeas, coconut milk, tomatoes and spices make a dinner from nothing.

guide.title: Cook once, eat twice
guide.text: Curries and roasted vegetables are often better the next day.

faq.question: What's the quickest dinner here?
faq.answer: The High-Protein Crispy Tofu Bowl takes 30 minutes; use the Under 30 min filter for more.

faq.question: Can I freeze these dinners?
faq.answer: Curries and soups freeze well. Each recipe has storage notes.

faq.question: Are the dinners filling without meat?
faq.answer: Yes — every dinner is built around legumes, tofu or whole grains.

name: Snacks & Desserts
meta_description: Gluten-free and vegan snacks and desserts — fudgy almond-flour brownies, no-bake energy bites and more.
intro: Sweet things and small bites made with real ingredients — almond flour, dates, nut butters and dark chocolate. Treats that happen to be gluten-free or vegan, not compromises.

guide.title: Use naturally sweet ingredients
guide.text: Dates, bananas and maple syrup sweeten with more flavour than plain sugar.

guide.title: Chill before cutting
guide.text: Brownies and bars cut cleanly after an hour in the fridge.

guide.title: Make snacks in batches
guide.text: Energy bites keep a week in the fridge and freeze for months.

faq.question: Are energy bites gluten-free?
faq.answer: With certified gluten-free oats, yes — that's why they're marked “GF option”.

faq.question: Why almond flour in brownies?
faq.answer: It's naturally gluten-free and keeps brownies fudgy and moist.

faq.question: Can I freeze brownies?
faq.answer: Yes, individually wrapped, for up to 3 months.
